Plot differential facet functioning

Source: R/api-plotting-dispatch.R
plot.mfrm_dif.Rd

Compare saved group contrasts as ordered bars, a heatmap, or a paired two-group scatterplot with optional marginal histograms. Read the analysis method and scale before interpreting the size of a difference.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_dif'
plot(x, type = c("summary", "heatmap", "scatter"), ...)

Arguments

x

A result from analyze_dff().

type

"summary" for ordered effects, "heatmap" for the interaction grid, or "scatter" for a paired two-group scatterplot with marginal histograms (groups, metric, marginal = c("auto", "histogram", "none"), ci_level, show_labels).

...

Named controls described below. All views accept draw = FALSE to return the ggplot object without printing. Controls for other views are rejected.

Value

Invisibly, a ggplot object carrying the underlying plot payload accessible via plot_data(). The summary's data component holds the displayed contrasts; the heatmap's matrix holds the plotted matrix; the scatterplot's table holds paired group values (X, Y) and marginal_histograms records bin counts when marginal histograms are shown. Views retain source rows in pairs, response matches (when available) in cases, and source settings in analysis_config. When supplied to analyze_dff(), the separate prospective interaction review is retained in comparison_review. Its states do not classify the displayed residual/refit effects; inspect its own model and weights. Retain the returned notes and unavailable values when exporting; a plot does not qualify new inference.

Summary controls

  • top_n = 30 limits displayed contrasts; sort_by is "abs_effect" (default), "effect", or "classification".

  • ci_level = NULL omits intervals. A level such as 0.95 requests approximate normal intervals from available linked-refit standard errors; residual comparisons require NULL.

  • effect_thresholds adds symmetric effect-size guide lines, not classification boundaries. effect_axis_label overrides the axis label.

  • preset is "standard", "publication", "compact", or "monochrome".

Heatmap controls

  • metric = "obs_exp" shows cell mean observed-minus-expected scores; "t" shows a descriptive scaled residual, not a t-test. These require the cell table from method = "residual". "contrast" shows the saved pairwise group contrasts, on the analysis method's scale.

Heatmap appearance

  • show_values = TRUE labels cells; value_digits = 2 controls rounding.

  • flag_threshold = NULL adds no flags. A non-negative value outlines cells at or above that absolute value; flag_color = "black" sets the border.

  • scale_limit = NULL uses the observed range. A positive value fixes symmetric color limits for comparing plots. It does not change saved values.

Read the figure with its source table

Summary labels follow Level | Group1 | Group2. Both summary bars and contrast heatmaps use Group1 minus Group2. A positive residual contrast means higher mean residual scores in Group1; a positive refit contrast means a larger facet location in Group1. With the usual difficulty/severity orientation, the latter means harder for Group1. Check the model's facet signs and rubric coding before interpreting either as favorable treatment.

plot_data(p, "pairs") retains the source rows, counts and analysis conditions. For summaries, PlotStatus distinguishes displayed rows, finite contrasts omitted by top_n, and unavailable contrasts. The last two do not mean zero or no differential functioning. If all contrasts are unavailable, the summary cannot draw points; inspect x$dif_table or a contrast heatmap. Heatmap cells with missing values remain missing. An observed-minus-expected cell mean can still be shown when its cell is below min_obs; inspect sparse. The scaled-residual and pairwise-contrast routes withhold such values.

N_Group1 and N_Group2 count retained response rows. Residual results also give distinct-Person counts, which need not be independent observations. plot_data(p, "cases") preserves residual response matches and exclusion reasons; it is NULL for refit results, which have no such response audit. Refit source rows instead report ScaleLinkStatus, ContrastComparable, fixed-target flags and subgroup linking details. A finite point or an adequate linking screen does not establish formal DFF inference. See mfrmr_linking_and_dff for the different linking screens.

Interpreting output

Bars are anchored at zero. Width corresponds to effect size on the contrast's native scale. For method = "residual", this is the observed-minus-expected average difference between groups, in score units. For method = "refit", this is the subgroup parameter difference on the fitted logit scale when linking support allows a comparable contrast. Residual differences do not isolate differential functioning. Linked refit intervals omit estimated-anchor uncertainty and cross-refit covariance.

See also

analyze_dff(), dif_interaction_table(), mfrmr_plot_migration

Examples

# Supplementary workflow: run explicitly to keep routine checks brief.
# example("plot.mfrm_dif", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Saved synthetic JML/RSM analysis of example_bias.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "bias-jml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit
diag <- example_fit$diagnostics
# Group labels from the same synthetic data used for the saved fit.
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data(example_fit$dataset)
dff <- analyze_dff(fit, diagnostics = diag,
                   facet = "Rater", group = "Group", data = ratings)
unique(dff$dif_table$ClassificationSystem)
p <- plot(dff, type = "summary", draw = FALSE)
comparisons <- plot_data(p, "pairs")
comparisons[, c("Level", "Group1", "Group2", "Contrast",
                 "N_Group1", "N_Group2", "PlotStatus")]
table(plot_data(p, "cases")$Reason)
plot_data(p, "notes")
p_scatter <- plot(dff, type = "scatter", draw = FALSE)
head(plot_data(p_scatter, "data"))
} # }
